SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT,
KALABURAGI IN MVC NO.613/2015 IN RESPECT OF ENHANCING THE AWARD AMOUNT AND PLEASED TO DISMISS MFA NO.200219/2019 FILED BY THE APPELLANT/INSURANCE COMPANY.
THESE APPEAL AND MFA CROB.

COMING ON FOR ADMISSION THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 4 MFA No.200219/2019  C/w MFA Crob.200029/2019  JUDGMENT
Since these two appeals are arising out of common judgment, they are heard and disposed of by this order.
2. While MFA No.200219/2019 is filed by the insurance company challenging the quantum, MFA Crob.No.200029/2019 is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
4. It is the case of the petitioner that on 08.07.2014, at about 4-30 p.m., while waiting for school bus he was standing on the left side of the road near Kori Siddeshwar school.

At that time, a Indica car bearing registration No.KA.25/P.1192 (hereinafter referred as "the offending vehicle") driven by its driver in high speed, in rash or negligent manner came and dashed against the petitioner.
As a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained severe injuries resulting in permanent partial disability.
Despite, prolonged treatment, he is not completely cured.
As owner and insurer, the respondents are liable to pay the compensation.
5. Though appeared through counsel, respondent No.1 did not file written statement.
6. Respondent No.2 filed written statement disputing that accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
Accident occurred due to the fault of the petitioner.
Though admitted that the offending vehicle was covered by a valid policy, respondent No.2 has alleged that at the time of accident, the driver was not holding a valid driving licence.

The nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment and that the petitioner has suffered permanent partial The Oriental Insurance Company vs Revansiddappa And Anr on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138850627/
3 disability is also disputed by respondent No.2.
7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
8. On behalf of the petitioner, his father is examined as P.W.1.
Two doctors are examined as P.W.2 and 3.
Exs. P.1 to 15 are marked.
9. On behalf of respondent No.2, Ex.R.1 is marked.

10. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition filed by the petitioner granting compensation in a sum of Rs.6,26,000/- with interest at 6% per annum and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same as detailed below:
 Sl.

No . Particulars Amount.
 a. pain and suffering already Rs.5,00,000/-
 undergone and to be  suffered in future, mental  and physical shock,
 hardship, inconvenience  and discomforts etc and  loss of amenities in life on  account of permanent  disability.
 b. Towards medical and Rs.1,06,000/-
 incidental expenses during  the period of  hospitalization 8 days.
 c. Discomfort, inconvenience Rs.20,000/-
 and loss of earnings to the  parents during the period  of hospitalization  Total Compensation Rs.6,26,000/-
11.
Challenging the quantum, respondent No.2 filed the appeal contending that the disability taken at 72% of the whole body is on the higher side.

In the case of Master Mallikarjun vs. Divisional Manger, The National Insurance Company Ltd. and Another1 (Master Mallikarjun's case), the Hon'ble ILR 2013 KAR 4891 Supreme Court held that up to 90% disability, compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- is to be awarded.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjun vs. Divisional Manger, The National Insurance Company Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the light of the same grant of Rs.5,00,000/- towards 72%
disability is on the higher side.
The compensation granted under the other heads is also on the higher side.

12. On the other hand, the petitioner has filed cross-objection contending that having regard to the nature of the injuries sustained, the whole body disability ought to have been taken at 100% and the Tribunal has erred in restricting it to 72% and prays to enhance the compensation.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for respondent No.2 and perused the records.
14. As on the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 6 years.
As evident from Ex.P.6, the petitioner has suffered fracture of shaft of right femur, rupture of urethra and urinary bladder.

He has taken treatment at Chirayu Hosapital, Kalaburagi and Indira Gandhi Institute of Child Hospital,
Bengaluru.

entities.text:
Indira Gandhi Institute of Child Hospital,
Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He has undergone surgery.
Taking into consideration the documents placed on record and in the light of testimony of P.W.2 and P.W.3, the Tribunal has correctly assessed the disability at 72%.
It does not call for any interference.
Based on Master Mallikarjun's case, the Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- for pain and suffering.
Based on medical bills, the Tribunal has granted Rs.1,06,000/- towards medical and incidental expenses.
For the inconvenience and loss of earnings to the parents, it has granted Rs.20,000/-.
This is also reasonable and does not call for interference.

15. Thus, from the above discussion, I hold that both the appeals are liable to be dismissed and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) Both the Appeals are dismissed.
(ii) Registry is directed to transmit the amount in deposit to the Tribunal.
(if already not withdrawn)
(iii) Send a copy of this order to the Tribunal.
